title: Berkshire 2014 letter: wonderful businesses, float, conglomerate capital allocation, and volatility vs risk
summary: Buffett's 50th-anniversary letter covers Berkshire's origins in a failed textile business, Munger's shift from cigar butts to wonderful businesses, insurance float economics, why the conglomerate form allocates capital efficiently, stock-acquisition discipline, a fortress balance sheet, and why diversified stocks beat dollar assets over decades.

principles.text: Buy wonderful businesses at fair prices, not fair businesses at wonderful prices; cigar-butt investing doesn't scale.
principles.quote: Forget what you know about buying fair businesses at wonderful prices; instead, buy wonderful businesses at fair prices.

principles.text: Volatility is not risk; for long-horizon investors, dollar-based assets are riskier than diversified stocks.
principles.quote: Volatility is far from synonymous with risk. Popular formulas that equate the two terms lead students, investors and CEOs astray.

principles.text: Float is a revolving fund, not just a liability, but its benefits can be drowned by poor underwriting.
principles.quote: But to think of float as strictly a liability is incorrect; it should instead be viewed as a revolving fund.

principles.text: Never issue shares in an acquisition worth more than the business received.
principles.quote: The intrinsic value of the shares you give in an acquisition must not be greater than the intrinsic value of the business you receive.

principles.text: Never risk what you need to chase what you want; keep ample real cash and avoid sudden-demand obligations.
principles.quote: In our view, it is madness to risk losing what you need in pursuing what you simply desire.

principles.text: A conglomerate can reallocate capital without taxes or friction, and can buy stock pieces of wonderful companies as an option.
principles.quote: At Berkshire, we can – without incurring taxes or much in the way of other costs – move huge sums from businesses that have limited opportunities for incremental investment to other sectors with greater promise.
